name: Classic Hodgkin lymphoma, nodular sclerosis type

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: WHO Classification of Tumors of Hematopoietic and Lymphoid Tissues

criteria.description: Presence of characteristic Reed-Sternberg cells or variants in lymph node biopsy
Histopathological evidence of nodular sclerosis with broad collagen bands dividing lymphoid tissue
Immunohistochemical positivity for CD15 and CD30 on Reed-Sternberg cells
Presence of painless lymphadenopathy, typically in mediastinal or cervical regions

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation of Reed-Sternberg cells with nodular sclerosis pattern and positive CD15/CD30 immunophenotyping
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Exclusion of other lymphoma subtypes and reactive lymphadenopathies is essential

searchTerms: neck lymph node swelling without pain

pathognomonic.notes: Often asymptomatic but may cause cough or dyspnea
searchTerms: abnormal mass in chest on X-ray or CT

common.symptomName: B symptoms (fever >38°C, night sweats, weight loss >10%)
searchTerms: fever, night sweats, and weight loss
classic systemic symptoms including fever and sweating
B symptoms like fever and weight loss
intense itch but no skin changes

common.notes: Secondary to bone marrow involvement or chronic disease
searchTerms: fatigue related to low red blood cells

common.notes: May be palpable on physical exam

searchTerms: pain in lymph nodes after alcohol intake
lymph node tenderness caused by drinking
cough caused by chest area mass

rare.notes: Due to compression by mediastinal mass

laboratory: Leukocytosis or leukopenia depending on disease stage
imaging: CT scan revealing nodal enlargement with nodular sclerosis pattern
other: Histopathology showing lacunar variant Reed-Sternberg cells
Immunohistochemistry positive for CD15 and CD30, negative for CD45

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of 'popcorn' cells instead of classic Reed-Sternberg cells
CD20 positive and CD15/CD30 negative immunophenotype
Strong CD30 positivity but ALK protein expression differentiates
Different clinical presentation and treatment response

redFlags: Rapidly enlarging lymph nodes with systemic symptoms
Unexplained persistent fever and night sweats
Development of superior vena cava syndrome
references: Swerdlow SH, Campo E, Harris NL, et al. WHO Classification of Tumours of Haematopoietic and Lymphoid Tissues. IARC; 2017.
National Comprehensive Cancer Network (NCCN) Guidelines for Hodgkin Lymphoma, Version 2.2024.
